profile: Same resolved persistent InnoDB owner and parent interpretations, utf8mb4, exact database and table names, empty SQL mode, and native referential checks enabled.
scope: A single ALTER TABLE adding one or more resolved foreign constraints and checked whole-field ordinary or unique secondary B-tree keys. The bounded baseline uses ordinary signed INT fields, an owner with an original clustered identity, native names, and default visibility. The initial form has additions and can be composed with checked removal only where separately validated.

roles.physicalIndexAddition: One named or native-named secondary addition on an exact owner. Retain ordered pinned field names and directions, effective uniqueness, and the allocated physical identity.
roles.foreignConstraintAddition: One checked native child-parent pair list with the resolved effect, name and support allocation.
roles.tableKeyAlteration: One exact owner, ordered closed key operations and policy. The original headings, index catalog, name occupancy, allocation input and constraint catalog are constructor-only validation facts.

rules: A new explicit key can supply child support if its leading whole directional fields match the foreign-key shape. Search the native candidate set across both written orders. Apply the native release's ascending interpretation of legacy direction tokens.
A prior implicit key of the exact requested width can be replaced. A longer matching prior implicit key can suppress a new generated candidate. A matching original explicit key remains stable.

New explicit supporting keys remove earlier implicit indexes that they supersede before allocating the successor names. Preserve surviving explicit keys and independently occupied constraint symbols. Later dropping an edge does not itself drop its physical key.

Allocate all surviving new physical names in written action order with a common occupied-name set. A generated index can acquire a suffix when a preceding action occupies its base name. A later explicit request for an occupied name fails. A key name can equal an independently allocated constraint symbol when no two physical keys claim the same native name.

Allocate at most the native physical key limit in the final catalog. Check all explicit referenced fields, positive supported arities and both native directional roles. Resolve the referenced parent against its eligible original keys, including when the parent equals the owner.

Output one original-role ALTER with exactly the ordered clauses and the native allocation form. Preserve the original distinction between explicit and automatic name selection when the server resolves additional names from the written order.
observations: Observe original and final typed native catalog entries, absolute identities, physical names, key kinds, complete ordered fields, directions and support allocations. Compare native warnings and specific refusal stages.

Observe row and constraint effects with distinct column values, nullable rows, independently supported fields, future referential actions and unique checks. Use matching reference identities and engine settings in the independent baseline and canonical execution.

Derive the Cartesian coordinate IDs independently of the generator. Preserve proposed role, prior support, allocation order and outcome through each positive public route and each typed negative route.
The seed schedule also observes the three typed edit roles together where a declared original foreign key can be removed.

exploration.variation: Vary explicit key length, included names, order, uniqueness, checked directions, generated symbol and physical name occupancy, relative matching prefix, relation identity, and nullable field cases.

faults: Ignore the direction of the ordered supporting columns.
Ignore the exact allocated physical name.
open: Physical index drops, renames, primary-key additions, cases with no original clustered identity, generated and prefix field encodings, nondefault visibility and algorithm combinations, and their mixed compositions remain tracked for extension.
The normative native predicate and closure must be linked to direct and analysis paths and independently measured on every registered release before the scope qualifies.
mode: Same resolved persistent InnoDB owner and parent interpretations, utf8mb4, exact database and table names, empty SQL mode, and native referential checks enabled.

Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/IndexAddition.role: Add an ordinary or unique whole-field secondary index under a mixed table key alteration.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/IndexAddition.structure: One persistent key owner, physical index name and role, a nonempty ordered full directional key, and a checked automatic naming flag.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/IndexAddition.conditions: The fields belong to the exact resolved owner and have signed INT roles. The declaration has an original clustered identity. The containing statement verifies direction, original and final name availability and the native automatic allocation.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/IndexAddition.meaning: Install the named B-tree with its exact role and terms, potentially providing child support to a new foreign constraint. A unique index compares whole ordered values with InnoDB nullable-key rules.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/IndexAddition.externalInterpretation: The original owner, headings, key roles and data have the corresponding external interpretation under the native stock profile.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/IndexAddition.sql: Render one ADD INDEX or ADD UNIQUE INDEX clause using the selected original automatic or explicit naming mode and exact ordered field directions.

Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/AlterForeignK.role: Apply one atomic ordered group of mixed foreign-key and ordinary or unique secondary index changes.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/AlterForeignK.structure: Exact persistent owner, checked ordered heterogeneous actions, implicit index replacement names, release and native physical policy.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/AlterForeignK.conditions: Require foreign-key addition and a distinct action. Resolve the starting owner and parent independently. Check the exact foreign pair rules, the starting constraint namespace, nested role ownership and the shared ordered physical allocation.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/AlterForeignK.meaning: Install explicit and implicit keys, retain valid unaffected metadata, and apply named referential effects. Index and constraint catalogs have independent names. An action can enable support irrespective of its position, and naming follows the native order.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/AlterForeignK.externalInterpretation: The fixture and output share exact owner and parent declarations and corresponding native key populations.
Schema/ForeignKey/Exchange/AlterForeignK.sql: Emit one qualified ALTER TABLE with all ordered clauses and effective algorithm and lock.

negative: Both public routes refuse each duplicate physical name in the finite catalog.
Direct inputs must bind every exact owner and field, supply a proper explicit secondary role and native automatic name, include original clustered identity, and preserve original parent support.
